I both agree and disagree. I believe the rules are the rules, because a political party is not necessarily a democracy. A rigged general election is a very different issue than a rigged primary. The parties hold primaries and caucuses to nominate someone to vote for. The party can do that (almost) any damn way they want, whether it represents the majority of the people or not. I believe the parties "rigging" elections is completely fair because a party is not government. Technically, anyone who meets the basic requirements can run for president.

However, pragmatically speaking, there are two parties in the US and their nominees are the only real choices for president. This means that the way nominees are chosen in the current party system is wrong and should be changed. Currently, primaries and caucuses technically don't chose the president, but realistically reduce the number of choices to two. I think democracy is actually a stupid idea, but as long as it is the system we want to have, we should have much more freedom of choice of representation than we currently have.

tl;dr: The problem is the big-picture party system, not the small-picture party inner-workings
